tagline: South from Burns past the marshes to Catlow Rim and Fields.
intro: From Burns the byway runs south on OR 205 over Wrights Point, with the Blue Mountains behind and Steens Mountain ahead, and crosses between Harney Lake and Malheur Lake into the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge, home to 320 bird species. Past Frenchglen it runs along Catlow Rim and ends at the ranching community of Fields.

This was cattle country early. Peter French arrived from California in 1872 with 1,000 head for his father-in-law, fenced the whole Blitzen River Valley for a herd that passed 40,000, and was shot dead in 1897, allegedly by a homesteader in a fencing dispute. The homesteader was acquitted.
season: TripCheck gives late spring through fall as the best time, and the road is passable year round.

moments.title: Narrows
moments.text: Postmaster Springer named the place after himself in 1889, it became Narrows in 1892, and an interpretive site now looks west over Mud Lake and Harney Lake.

moments.title: Frenchglen Hotel
moments.text: Restored and enlarged with Civilian Conservation Corps labor in the late 1930s, the hotel still puts up guests bound for the refuge and Steens Mountain.

moments.title: Catlow Rim
moments.text: The basalt face of the Steens fault block walls the east side of the valley, over 1,000 feet high at its south end, and wild horses and bighorn are often seen from the road.

practical: Services are few and far between.
